pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text: `fx_pnl_attribution` answers "how much of my P&L came from each currency pair?" It takes `fx_deltas` (P&L per unit move of each FX rate) and `fx_moves` (the realised move in each rate), and sums delta times move across currencies, with optional `currency_names` as labels. `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` answers a different question: "does my risk model's P&L track the full-revaluation P&L closely enough?" It takes a daily risk-theoretical P&L series (`risk_theoretical_pnl`) and a hypothetical P&L series (`hypothetical_pnl`), then checks their Spearman rank correlation and volatility ratio to assign a Basel traffic-light zone. Those thresholds are set by the Basel Committee and are not parameterised. So the first explains where P&L came from, while the second tests whether the model's P&L is a good enough match to the full-revaluation figure.

explain.text: `fx_pnl_attribution` breaks down the profit and loss from foreign exchange exposure across currency pairs. For each currency, it multiplies the P&L per unit move of that FX rate (`fx_deltas`) by the realised move in that rate (`fx_moves`), then adds the results. Because the contributions are additive, you can see how much each currency added to or took from the total. You can optionally pass `currency_names` to label the currencies; otherwise they default to `ccy_0` and so on.

when.text:
`fx_pnl_attribution` (FX Pnl Attribution) fits when you want to break a portfolio's FX P&L down by currency pair.

- You have the P&L per unit move of each FX rate (`fx_deltas`) and the realised move in each rate (`fx_moves`), and want to see how much each currency contributed.
- You want a total FX P&L that is additive across currencies, so the pieces sum to the whole.
- You want readable output: `currency_names` lets you label currencies instead of the default `ccy_0, ...`.
- Your question is about FX exposure in market risk reporting or explaining realised moves, not about other risk factors.

If you need a different component, `rates_pnl_attribution` is listed as interest-rate P&L attribution by key-rate tenor, and `credit_pnl_attribution` as credit P&L attribution by issuer / curve.
